This role will be offered on a 14-month fixed term contract, subject to availability of funding and will be based in Kampala, Uganda. This advert closes on 20 th October 2026. GAIN encourages early applications and reserves the right to close the advert ahead of the advertised deadline if we receive a high volume of interest. Key Responsibilities Include. Support the Project Manager in ensuring that all four project components - school meal menu improvement, food education and environments, market linkages, and policy engagement - function as an integrated package. Identify and maximize environmental co-benefits — working with the project team and partners to advance approaches that reduce environmental impact while supporting sustainable production and value chains for nutritious foods, and monitoring and reporting on those approaches Coordinating with millers, vegetable vendors, and MSMEs to formalize supply agreements and embed nutrition quality specifications into school procurement processes. In liaison with the Project Manager, supporting the contextualization and rollout of the Heroes Journey food education initiative within Ugandan schools. Facilitating accurate project budgeting and forecasting processes, ensuring that activities costs are kept within budgets. Support the Project Manager in developing Terms of Reference (ToRs) for project consultants/suppliers hired on a short-term basis. About You The ideal candidate will have practical experience supporting the delivery of nutrition, food systems, school feeding, education or related development programmes within Uganda. They should have experience coordinating project activities, working with schools, government structures, community stakeholders and private sector partners, and supporting implementation against agreed workplans, budgets and timelines. Experience in school food and nutrition programming, social and behaviour change activities, environmental or climate considerations, and donor-funded projects is required. Contribute analytical evidence to discussions and implementation of WFP assistance, including general food assistance, school feeding and resilience-based programmes. A post-secondary certificate in a related functional area is desirable. Experience: At least six years of progressively responsible experience, including relevant experience in assessments, data analysis, market monitoring, targeting or food security analysis. Knowledge & Skills Experience in conducting surveys, assessments and quantitative data analysis. Good understanding of household vulnerability analysis and targeting approaches. Proficiency in SPSS, R, STATA, Excel or other data analysis software. Ability to conduct and interpret statistical analysis, including regression analysis, and translate findings into clear recommendations. Strong report writing, data presentation and communication skills. Experience working with government counterparts and humanitarian or development partners. Other Post Requirements Previous experience in humanitarian or development contexts. Previous experience in conducting assessments, surveys or research. Experience in household-level data analysis, targeting, market monitoring or food security analysis. Good report writing and communication skills. This position will be in support of the Preventive Medicine and Biostatistics department at the University Services University of the Health Sciences located in Bethesda, MD. The Postdoctoral Research fellow will be working on a National Science Foundation (NSF) funded project that aims to build the first integrated phylogenomic, morphological, and ecological framework of the entire Anopheline mosquito subfamily. The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will lead genomic assembly and phylogenomic inference, contribute to 3D morphometric trait extraction and environmental niche modeling, and co-lead peer-reviewed manuscripts across multiple aims. The Iran Editor coordinates freelance contributors, develops enterprise stories, leads breaking-news coverage, curates a specialized newsletter, and contributes to video and podcasts. Maintain a diverse network of political, diplomatic, security, economic, and civil-society sources. Conduct interviews and protect sensitive sources through appropriate confidentiality and secure communication practices. Edit and verify articles, scripts, and source material for accuracy, balance, clarity, and publication readiness. Ensure content meets MBN editorial standards, sourcing requirements, and applicable legal requirements. Multiplatform and Bilingual Content Write and curate an Iran-focused newsletter and contribute to videos, explainers, podcasts, and live appearances. Deep knowledge of Iranian politics, regional security, nuclear diplomacy, economic conditions, and foreign relations. Strong editing and news judgment, with experience coordinating breaking news and editorial calendars. Fluency in Persian (Farsi) required, strong working proficiency in English required, professional proficiency in Arabic desirable. Experience producing digital newsletters, video scripts, and on-camera or podcast analysis. Strong understanding of reporting restrictions, digital verification, source protection, and safety practices relevant to Iran coverage. Background in nuclear diplomacy, security, sanctions, energy, or economic reporting. Experience coordinating freelance contributors and using open-source verification techniques.
